verdict.rationale: Buzz has its own per-agent credentials: each agent gets a separate Nostr keypair ("Mint a separate keypair for each") with "their own channel memberships, and their own audit trail." Access is scoped through channel membership. NIP-AA ties agent access to the owner's membership, so revoking the owner cuts off the agent automatically, and the git helper reuses the agent's keypair instead of a separate PAT. However, the scoping is membership-based rather than true least-privilege grants; community comments note channel-based scoping but do not contradict it. missing for 10: fine-grained capability/permission scopes per agent credential (e.g., read-only or per-action limits), credential expiry/rotation controls, independent hands-on corroboration of scoping in practice.
